$comment: Read by tools/ci/dependency-audit.mjs since 2026-10-25; audit-ci itself
was removed then. The file kept its name and format so the history below
still reads. Keys that only audit-ci understood (report-type,
package-manager, directory, show-found, show-not-found) were dropped, and
the script rejects any key it does not implement. What changed in how
the policy is applied: the Security workflow's PR gate fails only on an
advisory a change brings in, and the full list below the thresholds goes
to the `dependency-audit` issue from a daily run, never to a red check.
Inherited from the backend, where `security-check` was commented out of
pull-request.yaml, so this config had never actually gated anything.
MDRS-15 wires it into CI (.github/workflows/ci.yaml, `security` job).
package-manager was 'npm' and is now 'pnpm': the merged repo has a single
pnpm-lock.yaml and no package-lock.json anywhere, so the npm reader found
nothing to audit.
skip-dev was `true` (inherited) and is now `false`. With it on, `pnpm audit`
reported `devDependencies: 0` — all 1155 of them unaudited — so a new
critical in jest, nx, biome, drizzle-kit or testcontainers would have passed
the gate silently. That directly contradicted the property this file claims
to provide, so the cheaper fix (weaken the claim) was rejected in favour of
auditing dev dependencies too. Cost: 38 high instead of 28, across 31
advisories instead of 24.
The allowlist is a ratchet, not an amnesty. `audit-ci` on c59d467 reported
38 high / 27 moderate / 2 low / 0 critical over 1833 total dependencies,
and 31 GHSA IDs were allowlisted below to avoid red-lining every PR before
MDRS-21 could run.
MDRS-21 fixed 29 of the 31 with direct catalog bumps or pnpm.overrides
entries (see pnpm-workspace.yaml's Security floors section) — mostly
transitive next/postcss/sharp/@opentelemetry, plus js-yaml, uuid, nanoid,
fast-uri, qs, brace-expansion, file-type and esbuild at whatever depth
they were pinned. `pnpm exec audit-ci --config ./audit-ci.json` now finds
only the 2 that remain below.
xlsx@0.18.5 (both entries, GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6 and GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9) was
MDRS-8 FU-5: no patched xlsx exists on npm. It turned out not to need
replacing. apps/nizam stopped importing it on 2026-02-22, when the card
sample and export moved to tedrisat (exceljs, libs/common), and only the
package.json line was left behind. The dependency and both entries were
removed on 2026-10-25, which left this allowlist empty.
low and moderate stay ungated, as inherited.
GHSA-ch52-4w7c-c8xp (http-cache-semantics) and GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm
(braces) were allowlisted on 2026-10-03, when neither had a patched
release. Both entries were removed on 2026-10-25: http-cache-semantics
4.3.0 is fixed and cacheable-request's ^4.1.1 admits it, and braces was no
longer found in the lockfile at all.
